raw_response:
I'm fifty-two, been farming these 7.5 mu in Quzhou for thirty-five years. Middle school education — enough to read the fertilizer bags and understand what the extension fella says, but honestly I trust my own eyes more than any book. My old man taught me, and I've learned from every season since.

This year, like most years, it's cabbage and chili that pay the bills. That's my cabbage-chili system. The other crops fill in the gaps — eggplant brings decent money at the market, kidney beans are easy money in summer, and I keep half a mu of maize for our own cornmeal. Three mouths at home: me, my wife, and our son who works construction in the county town but comes back for the busy spells.

Money's tight. I probably have about six thousand yuan cash I can spend on inputs this year, and I need to stretch every bit of it. Fertilizer prices went up again, so I'm thinking hard about where to cut and where I absolutely cannot.

**Cabbage (2 mu):** I'm doing spring cabbage on two mu. Transplanted the seedlings in late March — bought hybrid苗 from Old Wang down the lane, costs me about 150 yuan per mu, but his苗 are sturdy. For fertilizer, I put down a base of 50 jin of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu, plus half a cart of chicken manure I saved from last autumn. That manure didn't cost me cash, just labor. Cabbage is a hungry crop. I'll topdress twice with urea — about 15 jin per mu each time — once when the heads start forming and once two weeks later. Last year I did three topdressings, but urea is 20% dearer this year, so I'll watch the plants. If they look dark green and vigorous after the second dressing, I'll save my money. Water — I'll irrigate four times: right after transplanting, at rosette stage, at heading, and one more depending on the rain. The well water isn't free, electricity for the pump adds up. For pests, cabbage worms and aphids always come. I'll spray when I see them, probably two or three times, using lambda-cyhalothrin and imidacloprid. I don't do preventive spraying — that's wasting money.

**Chili (2.5 mu):** This is where my labor goes. Chili seedlings went in mid-April. Seedlings cost about 200 yuan per mu, hybrid ones. Base fertilizer is 50 jin of compound and 30 jin of superphosphate per mu — the phosphorus helps with flowering. I'll topdress with urea twice: 10 jin per mu at pre-flowering and another 10 jin at peak fruiting. So about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu total. Chili needs water at the right times — too much and the roots rot, too little and the flowers drop. I'll irrigate five times, especially during the hot spells in July and August when the well runs longer. Pests are the worst on chili — thrips, whitefly, and anthracnose. I'll need insecticide and fungicide, probably three or four sprays this season. I hate spending on chemicals, but one bad virus year wiped out my neighbor's entire crop, so I don't take chances. Harvest is multiple picks from late July through October. I'll need to hire labor for picking — maybe 12 days total at 120 yuan a day. My wife and I can't do it all.

**Eggplant (1.5 mu):** Transplanted mid-April, similar timing to chili. Seedlings cost about 180 yuan per mu. I give it a bit less fertilizer than chili — 40 jin compound base, then two urea topdressings of 12 jin each. Eggplant is susceptible to red spider mite and wilt, so I'll spray insecticide and fungicide maybe three times. Irrigate four times. The picking goes on for months, so labor is steady. I'll hire maybe 5 days of help for the heavy harvest weeks.

**Kidney bean (1 mu):** Planted in mid-April by direct seeding. Bought new seed this year for 50 yuan per mu — my saved seed from last year looked a bit shriveled, didn't want to risk it. Beans fix some nitrogen, so I go lighter: 30 jin compound as base, one urea topdress of 10 jin at flowering. Irrigate three times. Maybe one insecticide spray if aphids show up. This is my easiest crop.

**Maize (0.5 mu):** Half a mu on the south corner, just for household eating. Planted mid-April. Using Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed — old reliable variety, 40 yuan per mu. 25 jin compound fertilizer as base, then one topdress of 15 jin urea at the big-flare stage. Irrigate twice, three times if the drought is bad. No pesticides — not worth it for half a mu of family corn.

Total costs I'm looking at: seeds around 1,100 yuan, fertilizers around 1,400 yuan, pesticides around 500 yuan, pumping electricity maybe 400 yuan, and hired labor about 2,000 yuan. That's roughly 5,400 yuan. I budgeted six thousand, so I've got a small cushion for if something goes wrong — and something always does. 

My yield expectations? If the weather cooperates and the market doesn't crash: cabbage around 3,500 kg/mu, chili around 2,000 kg/mu fresh, eggplant 3,500 kg/mu, kidney bean 1,200 kg/mu, and maize 450 kg/mu. But I've been doing this long enough to know that expectations are just hopes with numbers attached. What matters is getting through the season without a disaster, paying for my inputs, and having enough left to live on. My neighbor Zhang planted less chili last year and did well on cabbage; I'm watching him, but I'm not changing my whole plan. I'll stick to what I know, adjust at the edges, and hope the well doesn't run dry in August.
